evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §2 l.54-55: 'The page computes no figure a tp command reports: every count, state, rank, layout position and diff it shows arrives computed.' §13 l.302-303: 'what releasing the spec would do to the plan (the epics it frees, the gate it moves)'. §16 l.352-359 lists tp export's fields, and none is release impact. §2 l.60-63 lists the export additions, and no band counts are among them.
finding: §13's header shows 'what releasing the spec would do to the plan (the epics it frees, the gate it moves)', but no payload the spec defines carries it: §16's `tp export` lists sections, tasks, loops, the `tp resume` view, epic, `bound_at` and `imported_at`, and §2's additions to `tp epic export` carry nothing per file about release impact. §2 says every count, state and diff the page shows 'arrives computed'. So the page has to derive which epics a release unblocks and which gate it moves from the graph, which is a second derivation, or the spec owes a field nobody is told to add. The lifecycle band's stage-by-phase counts (§6) have the same gap: neither §2's export additions nor §17's per-day series carry them, so one implementation counts in JS and another adds a band to the export.
suggestion: Name where each one comes from: add a release-impact field (freed epic ids, gate moved) to `tp export` for a bound file, and the band's stage-by-phase counts to the export or the server push. Or state in §2 that counting rows of a payload the page was given is allowed, and drop release impact from §13 if no command will compute it.

evidence: Read spec/1.8.0.md lines 48-58 (§2: push set is tp epic export and tp export --list; 'every payload is produced in-process by the code the commands use') against line 397 (§17: 'The dashboard server computes the per-day series in Go and pushes it beside the export (§2)'); git diff --no-index --word-diff against snapshot-round-2.md shows both sentences changed in round 2.
finding: The round-2 repair of §17 has the dashboard server compute the per-day lifecycle series and push it 'beside the export (§2)', but §2, rewritten in the same round, enumerates what the server pushes as `tp epic export` (with a graph) and `tp export --list` only, applies the content-changed rule to those, and says 'every payload is produced in-process by the code the commands use' — the series is produced by no command. One implementation treats the series as a third pushed payload under the same change rule (it then changes at each day boundary); another embeds it in one of the two pushed payloads, which §2's list of export additions and §17's own removal of export fields forbid.
suggestion: Add the series to §2's push sentence ('and, with a graph, §17's per-day series, computed by the server from the export') under the same content-changed rule, and narrow 'every payload is produced by the code the commands use' to the command payloads.

evidence: Read spec/1.8.0.md lines 56-58 (§2 re-fetch rule) and lines 359-361 (§16: --list row fields) against §13 lines 297-313 (Read, Tasks, detail panel content); word-diff vs snapshot-round-2.md shows 'Its data is the payload of `tp epic export` and of `tp export` (§16)' replaced in round 2.
finding: Round 2 replaced 'its data is the payload of tp epic export and of tp export' with a GET of one spec's `tp export`, re-fetched 'when a push shows that file ... changed'. The only pushed per-file data is the `tp export --list` row (path, title, epic and state, phase, task counts, rounds, next step, escalation; §16). Many changes §13's Spec tab draws leave that row identical: an edit to the spec's text (Read view), a task's acceptance, estimate or dependencies, a `tp set` on a task, a task's state moving from 'waits on a task' to ready. The open Spec tab then shows stale content with nothing to trigger a re-fetch, which the old wording (the whole payload drove the push) did not allow. One implementation re-fetches only on a row change and goes stale; another re-fetches on every tick, which §2's Rejected clause on repeated per-tab work argues against.
suggestion: State what signals a file change: e.g. the --list row carries a content hash (or mtime) of the task file and its spec, and the page re-fetches when it changes; or say the server also re-derives the open file's `tp export` and pushes a changed marker.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §2 l.56-58: 'One spec's `tp export` (§16) ... it fetches by GET when it shows them, and again when a push shows that file or slice changed'. §16 l.359-361: '`tp export --list` prints one row per task file ...: path, title, epic and the epic's state, phase, task counts, review and audit rounds, the next step and any escalation'. None of these fields moves on an edit of the spec text or a task's acceptance.
finding: The Spec tab refetches one file's `tp export` only 'when a push shows that file ... changed', and the pushed payload for task files is `tp export --list`. Its rows carry path, title, epic state, phase, task counts, rounds, next step and escalation. Editing the spec text, a task's acceptance, estimate, description or dependencies, or `source_sections`, changes none of those fields. So the push never shows the change, and the open Spec tab keeps drawing stale sections and tasks until a reload. That breaks §2's live-data contract for the tab that draws the most per-file detail.
suggestion: Give each `--list` row a content revision of the file and its spec, or have the server also re-derive the shown file's `tp export` on the tick and push when it changes. Add a §18 row: an acceptance edit reaches an open Spec tab without a reload.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §2 L56-58: 'One spec's `tp export` (§16) ... it fetches by GET when it shows them, and again when a push shows that file or slice changed'. §16 L359-361 lists the --list row fields, none of which reflects spec text or task-field content.
finding: The page fetches one spec's `tp export` again 'when a push shows that file ... changed', but the pushed `tp export --list` row (§16: path, title, epic and its state, phase, task counts, review and audit rounds, next step, escalation) changes on none of these: an edit to the spec text, to a task's acceptance, description or estimate, or a `tp set` that leaves counts and phase alone. One implementation refetches only when the file's list row differs, so the open Spec tab's Read and Tasks views stay stale after such an edit. Another refetches on every push or adds a revision to the row. A test that edits the spec text with the Spec tab open passes one and fails the other.
suggestion: Give each `tp export --list` row a content revision (for example a hash over the task file and its spec) that the push comparison and the page's refetch both read, or state that the open spec is refetched on every push; add an acceptance row that a spec-text edit reaches an open Read view.

evidence: §2: 'One spec's `tp export` (§16) ... it fetches by GET when it shows them, and again when a push shows that file or slice changed'. §16: '`tp export --list` prints one row per task file ...: path, title, epic and the epic's state, phase, task counts, review and audit rounds, the next step and any escalation' — no field moves on a text or acceptance edit.
finding: The page re-fetches one spec's `tp export` only 'when a push shows that file ... changed', but the only per-file payload pushed is the `tp export --list` row, whose fields (path, title, epic and its state, phase, task counts, review and audit rounds, next step, escalation) do not change when the spec text, a task's acceptance or description, or a dependency is edited. An open Spec tab (Read and Tasks views) therefore stays stale through exactly the edits a review round makes, and two implementations disagree: one adds a per-file revision to the list row, the other re-fetches on every tick.
suggestion: Give each `--list` row a content revision of the file (and its spec) and say the page re-fetches when that revision changes; likewise name what in the export marks a slice's history as changed.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §2 line 62-63: "per bound file `bound_at`, `imported_at` (§15) and its tasks' earliest `started_at` (§17)"; §17 line 397: "The dashboard server computes the per-day series in Go and pushes it beside the export (§2)."; §16 line 354-355: every task with its "... times, closing evidence and commits".
finding: `tp epic export` gains, per bound file, its tasks' earliest `started_at`, but the only reader named for it is §17's lifecycle chart, and §17 has the dashboard server compute that per-day series in Go and push it beside the export. The page never reads the field, and an agent that needs a task's start already gets it from `tp export` (§16 carries every task's times). Every agent reading `tp epic export` pays for a key that feeds no decision.
suggestion: Drop the earliest `started_at` from `tp epic export`'s bound-file rows; the server derives it from the task files in-process when it computes §17's series.

evidence: §2: 'every count, state, rank, layout position and diff it shows arrives computed. It may filter, sort and search what it was given'. §2's list of `tp epic export` additions: generated_at, layout, lint, per-milestone §6 state, per-slice §5 fields, per-file bound_at/imported_at/started_at — no band counts. §6: 'The export carries this state per milestone' (milestone state only). internal/cli/epic_export.go: epics[] carry `status`, files[] carry `phase`, no stage×phase totals.
finding: §2 says every count the page shows arrives computed, but no payload §2 lists carries the lifecycle band's counts (§6: work epics per stage × earliest spec phase, task files per phase without a graph) or the strip's 'epics that changed stage' tally; the export carries per-epic `status` and per-file `phase`, so the band can only be produced by the page counting them. One implementation adds band counts to `tp epic export` (a contract change §2's additive list does not name), another counts in JS, which §2 forbids.
suggestion: Either add the band's stage×phase counts to the export additions in §2/§6, or state in §2 that counting given rows by a given field is allowed (as filtering is) and name the band as such.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §5 line 123-124: "The export's `slices[]` carry the same, and each recorded round's finding count, total and by role, in round order."; §11 line 264-265: "`tp epic review <slice> --history` prints the slice's rounds, each with its findings by role"; skills/tp/SKILL.md line 797 lists `tp epic export` with no `--compact` mode; §17 line 397 shows the pattern of a dashboard-only series "pushe[d] beside the export".
finding: The export's `slices[]` gain each recorded round's finding count, total and by role, in round order. That is the same per-round findings-by-role that §11's `tp epic review <slice> --history` prints, and its only consumer is the page's per-slice curve. `tp epic export` has no `--compact`, so every agent call carries slices x rounds x roles of history that feeds no agent decision: grant-round is the operator's (§7), and an agent asking whether a slice converges has `--history`.
suggestion: Keep the per-round series out of `tp epic export`: the dashboard server derives it from the same code as `--history` and pushes it beside the export, as §17 does for the lifecycle series. Keep in the export only what `--status` reports (cap, grants, stale unit ids, open findings by role).

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §2 L54-55: 'The page computes no figure a tp command reports: every count, state, rank, layout position and diff it shows arrives computed.' §2 L60-63 lists the export's additions without the band. §6 L144-147 defines the band's counting rule. internal/cli/epic_status.go:32 `Counts map[string]int json:"counts"` per milestone shows tp already reports epic counts.
finding: The lifecycle band's counts have no producer. §6 defines them by a derivation rule ('an epic with several bound specs counts once, at its earliest phase'; unbound files count only with no graph), but §2's list of what `tp epic export` gains carries per-milestone state, layout, lint, slice fields and per-file times, and no band counts; §17's server-side series covers the over-time chart, not the band. One implementation counts in the page from epics[].status and files[].phase, which breaks §2's 'The page computes no figure a tp command reports' (tp epic status already reports per-milestone `counts`) and makes the page run the earliest-phase ordering. Another adds a band field to the export that §2 does not list. Their tests disagree on whether the export carries the band.
suggestion: Add the band (stage counts and phase counts, with the earliest-phase and no-graph rules applied) to §2's list of export additions, or to the server's push beside the export as §17 does for the series, and add an acceptance row checking the export's band against a fixture where one epic has two bound specs at different phases.

evidence: §7: 'gates whose non-deferrable members are done awaiting `--met`; gates whose threshold is a placeholder (§8)'. §8: 'An absent or empty threshold is not reported: such a gate goes green once its members are done'. internal/engine/epicgate.go RecordGateMet: `if gate.Threshold == "" { return &GateMetRefusedError{... "the gate has no threshold"} }`.
finding: 'gates whose non-deferrable members are done awaiting `--met`' does not exclude a gate with no threshold, for which `--met` is refused and which is already green once its members are done (§8), nor say whether a gate with a placeholder threshold and its members done is listed once with the threshold rewrite, once with `--met`, or twice. Two implementations list different rows, and one of them offers a command tp refuses.
suggestion: Say the `--met` row is for an unmet gate with a written, non-placeholder threshold whose non-deferrable members are done, and that a placeholder gate appears only with the command that rewrites its threshold.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §13 line 304-305: "every section and paragraph carries a stable anchor (`§3 ¶2`) for the feedback a later release adds"; §16 line 353-354: "the spec's text in numbered sections, each section and paragraph with its anchor"; Non-goals line 437: "Feedback on the spec (the anchors are left for it)".
finding: Each paragraph of the full `tp export` payload carries its own anchor string, but the anchor shown (`§3 ¶2`) is the section's number and the paragraph's position, which the array's order already gives. Its stated purpose is feedback that a later release adds, which is listed as a non-goal. The bytes repeat once per paragraph of every spec read without `--compact`.
suggestion: Emit the section number with each section and the paragraphs as an ordered array without per-paragraph anchor strings; the anchor is section number plus index. Add an explicit anchor field when the feedback release defines anchors that are not positional.

evidence: Read spec/1.8.0.md lines 400-402 ('tasks closed (from `tp export --list`'s counts)') and line 411 (acceptance 'a reload shows it in the strip').
finding: Round 2 made the strip's 'tasks closed' come from `tp export --list`'s counts, so the strip can say how many tasks closed per file, not which. The acceptance still reads 'After a task closes in another terminal, a reload shows it in the strip', which a tester can read as the task itself (id or title) appearing, which the counts cannot supply.
suggestion: Reword the acceptance: 'a reload shows that file's closed-task count rising by one in the strip'.

evidence: §17: 'The dashboard server computes the per-day series in Go and pushes it beside the export (§2).' §2: re-derives 'tp epic export ... and tp export --list' and pushes 'only when its content changed'. §18 row 3: 'an unchanged repository pushes nothing after the first state'.
finding: The per-day lifecycle series is pushed 'beside the export', but §2's change-only push rule covers only the two re-derived exports, and a series that runs to the current day changes at midnight in an unchanged repository, which §18 row 3's 'an unchanged repository pushes nothing after the first state' forbids if the series is in the compared content.
suggestion: State whether the series is part of the compared content and whether it ends at the last recorded time or at today.

evidence: spec/1.8.0.md §7 l.163-165: 'gates whose non-deferrable members are done awaiting `--met`; gates whose threshold is a placeholder (§8)'. §8 l.188: 'a placeholder is a threshold the operator has not written'.
finding: A gate whose non-deferrable members are done and whose threshold is a placeholder matches two §7 categories. It is listed as awaiting `--met` and also as a placeholder to rewrite. The list then offers `--met` for a gate whose threshold §8 says the operator has not written, inviting a gate marked met against `TBD`. The spec does not say whether the placeholder row replaces the `--met` row or stands beside it.
suggestion: State that a gate with a placeholder threshold is listed only under the placeholder row, with the `tp epic set` command, until its threshold is written.

evidence: Read spec/1.8.0.md lines 202-204 (§9 tie-break) and line 427 (§18 row 8).
finding: The round-2 tie-break gives a tie between equally long chains 'to the chain whose milestones come first in the graph file', which does not say how two chains are compared: by their first milestone (equal when both start at the same track root), by their first differing milestone, or by the earliest milestone anywhere in the chain. §18 row 8's fixture of two equally long chains may pass under one comparison and fail under another.
suggestion: Say 'compared milestone by milestone from the root, the first differing milestone earlier in the graph file wins'.
